name: X-ray room
description: Plain X-rays: chests, limbs and joints. Patients are brought here from A&E and a radiologist reports the film.
staffing: Hire a radiographer from Recruitment (H) to run it.

name: CT scanner
description: CT scans of the head and chest: finds bleeds on the brain, strokes and blood clots in the lungs.
staffing: Hire a radiographer from Recruitment (H) to run it.

name: Operating theatre
description: Emergency operations: appendicectomy, ectopic pregnancy and hip fractures. Patients recover on a ward afterwards.
staffing: Hire a consultant surgeon from Recruitment (H). Tick which departments may use it in the room panel.

name: Anaesthetic room
description: Every operating theatre needs one. Build it against the theatre's wall: automatic doors join the two. The anaesthetist puts each patient to sleep here, then wheels them straight through onto the table, so the next patient can be got ready while the theatre is cleaned.
staffing: No staff of its own: the theatre's anaesthetist works here. Must share a wall with a theatre.

name: Recovery room
description: Bays where patients wake up after their operation, each behind its own curtains, with a recovery nurse for every two bays. Without a free bay they wake up on the theatre table, and the theatre can't start its next case until they have.
staffing: Recovery nurses: one for every two bays, day and night.

name: Pharmacy
description: Buys medicines at list price. A&E and clinic patients going home collect their prescriptions at the counter (working-age adults pay the £10 charge), and a porter carries ward patients' medicines to take home up to the ward. Without one, medicines cost 50% more, ward discharges wait about 4 hours and prescriptions go to a chemist in town.
staffing: Hire a pharmacist from Recruitment (H) to run it.
